sections.executive_summary: Original Blue detected the audited taxonomy attacks in the frozen Gate B traffic, but missed some audited free-play attempts. Open Blue detected more attempts in the free-play replay and produced more false alarms in the sealed benign prompt check. Those comparisons are tentative. The layered option has not been tested.
sections.methodology: Red sent requests through a logging proxy. Blue labelled requests from the log after traffic was sent, and a code-based Judge scored rounds. The designer audited labels for selected detection measures. Free-play detection counts any attack label and excludes ordinary browsing. Open Blue was evaluated by replay, not live. The sealed benign check tested the prompts without rules.
sections.results: The findings distinguish detection from challenge landing and false alarms. Replays test configurations on existing traffic; they do not show how those configurations would affect future traffic.
sections.risk_register: Prompt-scope blindness: Original Blue's attack definition is narrower than the attack space. Application-context blindness: Blue does not know what the site links to, so forced browsing can read as ordinary traffic. Structural blindness: Some detection requires user identity, as in access control; this was not tested here.
sections.deployment_options: A is Original Blue. B is Open Blue. C is Layered: Original Blue supplies high-priority alerts and Open Blue supplies a low-priority queue. C is untested.
sections.decision_criteria: The choice depends on the value placed on alert precision, broader coverage, workload and evidence from a tested configuration. The decision is human.
sections.limitations: The evidence is limited to the frozen application traffic and the specified configurations. The free-play audit is a designer assessment, and the detection comparison is tentative. Deepseek taxonomy labels were not audited. Challenge landing is not the same as detection. The summary does not quantify run-to-run verdict variation or test the layered deployment.

findings.text: Original Blue flagged {{gate_b.detection}} of audited Gate B attack rounds; the interval was {{gate_b.detection.ci}}. Orphans and instrument failures were excluded. Among rounds with measurable landing, {{gate_b.landed}} solved their mapped challenge.

The unaudited deepseek taxonomy results were {{gate_b_deepseek.detection}} without the evasion directive and {{gate_b_evasion.detection}} with it. These results are tentative because Red's labels were not audited.

In free play, the designer audited {{freeplay_original.attack_attempts}} rounds as attack attempts among {{freeplay_original.rounds}} rounds. Original Blue detected {{freeplay_original.detection}} of those attempts; the interval was {{freeplay_original.detection.ci}}. Challenge landing occurred in {{freeplay_original.landed_rounds}} rounds. The detection estimate is tentative.

On replay of the same free-play traffic, Open Blue detected {{freeplay_open.detection}} of audited attack attempts; the interval was {{freeplay_open.detection.ci}}. The change was {{freeplay.open_detection_change_vs_original}}. This comparison is tentative. Open Blue still missed some enumeration and directory-listing attempts in this traffic.

On sealed benign requests with rules disabled, the original prompt flagged {{fp_check_original.fp}}; the interval was {{fp_check_original.fp.ci}}. The open prompt flagged {{fp_check_open.fp}}; the interval was {{fp_check_open.fp.ci}}. The observed change was {{fp_check.open_fp_change_vs_original}}. The open-prompt result and comparison are tentative.

On Gate B replay, Sonnet with the library detected {{gate_c_sonnet.detection}} of audited attack rounds, and Haiku with an empty library detected {{gate_c_haiku_empty.detection}}. Both matched the original Gate B detection figure in this traffic. This does not establish equivalence on other traffic.

On M5 traffic, the library configuration detected {{m5_library.detection}} of audited attack rounds, matching the empty-library and rules-off configurations. Its total AI call count changed by {{m5.calls_change_vs_empty_library}} and {{m5.calls_change_vs_rules_off}}. Its total AI cost changed by {{m5.cost_change_vs_empty_library}} and {{m5.cost_change_vs_rules_off}}. The call and cost comparisons are tentative and cover every agent.

strengths: The original prompt produced no observed false alarms in the sealed benign check.
Wider coverage in the free-play replay.
weaknesses: More false alarms in the sealed benign check.
Verdicts vary run to run; the summary does not quantify that variation.

options.summary: Layered: Original Blue as high-priority alerts, Open Blue as a low-priority queue.
strengths: Separates the alert streams by priority.
weaknesses: The low-priority queue may add review work.

criteria.if_you_value: Precision and a tested original configuration
criteria.because: The original prompt produced no observed false alarms in the sealed benign check, though it missed free-play attempts outside its taxonomy.

criteria.if_you_value: Broader coverage and can accept more false alarms and variable verdicts
criteria.because: Open Blue detected more audited attempts in the tentative free-play replay comparison, while the open prompt produced more false alarms in the benign check.

criteria.if_you_value: Separating high-priority alerts from a broader review queue
criteria.because: The layered design assigns those roles to the original and open configurations, but its combined performance and workload are untested.
